intended_object: The canonical natural isomorphism map(F ⋙ G) ≅ map F ⋙ map G. It says that the construction C ↦ C ⊳ (adjoining a terminal object) respects composition of functors, as part of its (pseudo)functoriality. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The definition builds the isomorphism componentwise: on an object `of X` and on `star`, the two functors agree definitionally, so every component is the identity isomorphism. Naturality is discharged automatically by `cat_disch`. This is exactly the standard compositor isomorphism for the functor C ↦ WithTerminal C.

It is stated at full generality: arbitrary categories C, D, E and arbitrary functors F and G, with universe-polymorphic objects and morphisms. No assumption is restricted.

It is the basic coherence datum belonging to this construction, and Mathlib does not state it more generally elsewhere. The analogous `WithInitial.mapComp` is the dual statement, not a generalization of this one.
